title: Efficient bias mitigation in T2I diffusion models using Concept Graphs
claim: Methods that correct only one component yield incoherent or biased outputs; aligning all components jointly gives coherent, balanced results.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dashed dividers, output image columns with colored borders
description: Three side-by-side panels, separated by dashed vertical lines, each showing the same text-to-image pipeline: prompt P flows into an orange Encoder trapezoid, a blue Denoiser box, and a green Decoder trapezoid, then fans out into three generated image samples. In the left panel a wrench icon sits on the Encoder (text-encoder-only fix); the outputs are garbled, text-like images, with red borders and the label 'Inconsistent Output'. In the middle panel the wrench sits on the Denoiser; the outputs are female nurses with red borders, labeled 'Negated denoiser correction'. In the right panel, CO-ALIGN, a pink box encloses Encoder and Denoiser with a wrench on top. Below it are three small colored concept graphs labeled CG Txt Enc, CG GT and CG Denoiser. Its outputs have green borders, show diverse nurses, and are labeled 'Coherent and unbiased output'. Red versus green borders and labels draw the eye first.
caption: Existing bias mitigation methods that intervene on only the text encoder (left) or denoiser (centre) produce either semantically incoherent outputs or gender-biased generations for the prompt “Nurse”. CO-ALIGN (right) jointly aligns the concept graphs of both components toward a target
abstract: Text-to-Image diffusion models often propagate harmful bias inherited from the training data. Existing bias mitigation techniques typically intervene only at the text encoder or provide inference-time guidance, often leading to generations that collapse into semantically incoherent outputs. To address these limitations, we introduce CO-ALIGN (Concept Ontology Alignment), a novel bias mitigation approach based on concept-graph alignment that operates on the model's internal concept ontology. By aligning concepts within the text encoder and denoiser, CO-ALIGN achieves substantial bias reduction while preserving generative integrity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of concept-graph alignment across three paradigms: text-encoders, denoisers and joint text-denoiser ontology alignment. CO-ALIGN outperforms the state of the art, improving fairness by $30\%$, $ÎFID=11.4$ in image quality, $2.8\%$ in image fidelity, all while reducing semantically incoherent outputs by $88\%$. Beyond bias mitigation, we show that CO-ALIGN benefits other downstream tasks as well. In particular, our experiments demonstrate that better-aligned internal ontologies enhance concept unlearning robustness across multiple unlearning techniques.
